pr_title: Allow specify dynamic templates in bulk request
pr_comments: @javanna Thank you for the review. I tweaked the API using "match_mapping_hint" and I found it's simpler and less confusing. I have updated the PR. Can you take another look?
@dnhatn apologies if this is obvious: will this be immediately usable through an Ingest script processor (and if so how?), or would that come later?

> can users use one of these types as hint in their bulk requests, in which case they won't have to do define anything on the dynamic template side of things? Or should hints always be arbitrary and explicitly defined in the dynamic template?

That's a good question. Let's discuss it after this iteration.

Agreed with @javanna that this looks great. I'm happily surprised with the low number of new lines of codes that this PR adds!

One thing I wonder about the API is whether we actually need a new parameter in dynamic templates, or if we could reuse the dynamic template name. For instance the example from the issue description uses about the same name for the template name and for the mapping hint, which looks like a good practice to me. Should we go further and match the index request's `mapping_hints` on dynamic template names rather than on their `match_mapping_hint`? We could change the parameter name to something like `dynamic_template_names` or `dynamic_template_name_hints` to make the connection clearer if we thought this is a better API.

Another thing I wonder is what is the right behavior in case of conflict between these hints and existing options of dynamic templates like `match_mapping_type` and `path_match`. For instance, say you have a dynamic template configured with `match_mapping_type: object` and then create an index request that is configured to use this dynamic template on a string field. My understanding of the current code is that we would ignore _all_ dynamic templates in such a case, even if there is one that matches on `match_mapping_type:string`. This behavior goes a bit against the intuition I have for a `hint`, which is that things should behave as if there had been no hint provided if there isn't a match, ie. we should take the template that matches on `match_mapping_type:string` rather than ignoring all dynamic templates? Having precedence rules in docs before merging would help me better think through these cases.

> One thing I wonder about the API is whether we actually need a new parameter in dynamic templates, or if we could reuse the dynamic template name

that is a great idea, I wonder how I did not see that myself , thanks for bringing it up :)  I think that removes one level of indirection which is not needed. I would then use something like `dynamic_template_hints`. I suppose that `template_hints` is too short and unclear...

> Another thing I wonder is what is the right behavior in case of conflict between these hints and existing options of dynamic templates like match_mapping_type and path_match

I agree. I just realized that I am not entirely clear on the current behaviour, so maybe more testing would help identifying what is more sensible from a user perspective.

@jpountz Thanks for chiming in :).

I will update the PR to use the dynamic template name instead.

> My understanding of the current code is that we would ignore all dynamic templates in such a case, even if there is one that matches on match_mapping_type:string.

We will throw an exception in this case and fail the related item of a bulk request. I think that's a good behavior? WDYT?

> We will throw an exception in this case and fail the related item of a bulk request. I think that's a good behavior? WDYT?

Oh right, sorry for the noise! I wonder if there are cases when this will not be practical, e.g. if the data shipper doesn't have full control over the data that gets indexed, maybe @axw has thoughts on this.

>>> My understanding of the current code is that we would ignore all dynamic templates in such a case, even if there is one that matches on match_mapping_type:string.
>>
>> We will throw an exception in this case and fail the related item of a bulk request. I think that's a good behavior? WDYT?
>
> Oh right, sorry for the noise! I wonder if there are cases when this will not be practical, e.g. if the data shipper doesn't have full control over the data that gets indexed, maybe @axw has thoughts on this.

Not sure I follow the above. Are we saying that if a hint is specified that matches no dynamic template, then the document will be failed if it _does_ match some other dynamic template rule?

That would be fine for our use case, as we only have a fairly limited set of dynamic templates that shouldn't match any fields for which we'll use hints. Although we don't know the field names ahead of time, we still control when hints will be applied, and there are some restrictions on the field names. Namely, they shouldn't collide with any well-defined fields like those in ECS, which is where we have path_match rules in place. If a user specifies a metric/field name that collides, which would lead to a hint that conflicts with a path_match, then IMO it's reasonable for the document to be failed.

However, I don't find this behaviour intuitive from the word "hint".

> Are you suggesting "hints" should be optional?

No, I was only commenting on the intuitiveness of the naming. Behaviour-wise, I would prefer to have strict control over how something is dynamically mapped: if a "hint" (dynamic template name) is specified and no such dynamic template exists, then fail the document. Maybe it could be made optional? Fail vs. fall back to existing dynamic template matching rules?

heya @dnhatn based on the conversation around "conflicts" and behaviour above, I am thinking that it would be beneficial to work on the docs as part of this PR and highlight these different scenarios. Possibly also expand testing to cover those same scenarios. Would that work for you?
@javanna Sure, I will add docs and conflict tests in this PR.

@javanna @jpountz  

I've updated the PR to use the dynamic template name as we discussed. 
Two notes on the implementation:

- Dynamic templates without match conditions are now [allowed](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/58af624d32f6672d3762832bc95b6b0110e96a94/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/mapper/RootObjectMapper.java#L393-L398). Without this, dynamic templates can't be used exclusively for the name hints. We need to add some conditions to prevent a template from matching anything except fields used with the name hints.

- When using the name hints, other match conditions of a template are [ignored](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/58af624d32f6672d3762832bc95b6b0110e96a94/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/mapper/DynamicTemplate.java#L259-L262) because users explicitly "choose" the template.

Would you please take another look? Thank you!
@javanna I am happy with the current shape of the API. It's less confusing the previous iterations. Thank you so much for your feedback. I think I have addressed all your points.
I opened #70805 to discuss the mixed cluster version scenario more generally, and mention this PR as an example to see whether we are on the right track.
We reached some conclusion on https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/70805#issuecomment-805805047 . Do you have thoughts on this @dnhatn ?

issue_context.title: Give bulk requests the ability to give hints to dynamic mappings
comments: If we have this feature, we could standardise on some `match_mapping_types` names and use the in the `metrics-*-*` base template. This would mean most metric ingestion with type hints just work out of the box.
Thank you very much @dnhatn . This histogram feature will greatly help observability!

review_comments: do we need to open an issue for this?
I will work on it right after this PR.

you plan on backporting this to 7.x right? I was wondering what the ideal behaviour should be in a mixed cluster scenario. What happens here is that effectively the dynamic_templates section may be ignored depending on the version of the nodes holding the shard, which sounds surprising maybe for users? Do we have alternatives?
Yes, I think we should reject such requests. I added that BWC logic in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/69948/commits/b341fcc70c4baf5c631a1b74ac492878b30054e6.

relaxing this makes sense to me. I wonder though about the behavior in a mixed cluster, where only new nodes can support the newer format, and older nodes would not accept it. I assume things will fail, but where and how?
ok, can you remind me how the index created version relate to the node version?

It's the [smallest](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/321f46e1877d40d987294f28362619a322d92af3/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/MetadataCreateIndexService.java#L673) version of non-client nodes.
@javanna I pushed https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/69948/commits/aef927e301f68b67ea3f44a3a1cbaee866377b17 to use the min node version of the current state instead.
